characterization_methods: Optical band gap analysis via transmittance measurements
evidence: Scanning electron microscope images of an ALCVD indium sulphide layer on CIGS are shown in Fig. 2. Grazing-incidence X-ray analysis on a 200-nm indium sulphide layer on glass (Fig. 3) indicates a b-In S -type23 structure. The optical band gap of indium sulphide by ALCVD was determined by analysis of transmittance measurements of approximately 40-nm indium sulphide films on glass substrate. Fig. 5 shows the quantum efficiency measured on small-area devices with different buffer layer thicknesses compared to standard devices with a cadmium-sulphide buffer layer. The current–voltage curve is shown in Fig. 8. Annealing at 200 8C in air of laboratory cells with an indium sulphide buffer deposited at 160 8C led to an improvement of the device parameters. The open-circuit voltage and fill factor decrease slightly. In order to test the long-term stability of the cadmium-free mini-modules (5=5c m ), accelerated life-time tests2 are performed (Fig. 9).
